notes: §1985:XVI.1.4.3 GR2: an independent segment is in its initial state when control reaches it by 'the implicit transfer of control between a SORT or MERGE statement, in a segment with a different segment-number, and an associated input or output procedure in that independent segment'. A SORT/MERGE procedure runs as a nested __Dispatch call; EmitDispatchMethod saves the caller's __seg, and the loop's __SegOf[__pc] != __seg test calls __EnterSegment (AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitSegmentState) on the procedure's first pc, resetting its ALTERed GO TOs, while the finally restores the caller's segment (last-used on return). The witness runs one SORT twice with an INPUT PROCEDURE in SECTION 60 and sees FIRST twice; probe seg1 at 85 did the same for an OUTPUT PROCEDURE in SECTION 70 (OUT-INIT, OUT-ALT, OUT-INIT, OUT-ALT), and seg4 showed a procedure in the statement's own segment is not reset. Classes a, d, f do not reach the rule; c: the segment-number is COBOL0902 at 2002.

next.reason: 1985: "Control is transferred to that segment as the result of the implicit transfer of control between a SORT or MERGE statement"; 2023: "No Segmentation module or independent segments; candidates give only general SORT/MERGE implicit transfer of control (14.6.3)". The rule says when an independent segment is entered in its initial state. 2023 has no segments, and no candidate covers segment state, so the requirement is gone.
